title: Input and maths
bridge: Java reads typed input with a **Scanner**: `Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in);` then `in.nextLine()` (a line of text) or `in.nextInt()`. Watch division: `7 / 2` is 3 when both are ints (whole division, like Python's `//`); make one a double (`7 / 2.0`) to get 3.5. `%` is the remainder, as in other languages.
lesson:
To read what someone types, Java uses a **Scanner**:

```
import java.util.Scanner;

Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in);
String name = in.nextLine();               // a whole line of text
int age = Integer.parseInt(in.nextLine()); // a line, turned into a number
```

(There's also `in.nextInt()`, but mixing it with `nextLine()` leaves a stray newline behind; reading lines and converting is simpler and safer.)

Maths: `+ - * /` and `%` (remainder). **Watch division:** if both numbers are `int`, Java does whole division: `7 / 2` is `3`. If either is a `double`, you get `3.5`. This catches everyone once: `int a = 7, b = 2; double avg = a / b;` gives 3.0, because the division happened in ints first. Fix: `(double) a / b`.

`Math` has the extras: `Math.round(x)`, `Math.ceil(x)` (round up), `Math.floor(x)`, `Math.max(a, b)`, `Math.sqrt(x)`, `Math.pow(2, 10)`. To show a number with 2 decimals: `String.format("%.2f", value)` or `System.out.printf("%.2f%n", value)`.

notes: Make a Scanner on the keyboard.
Read a line, trim spaces, convert.
Whole division and remainder split minutes.

exercises.title: Shillings to dollars
exercises.prompt: Read a whole number of shillings, then the rate (may have decimals). Print the dollars with 2 decimals, like: 1300 KSh = 10.00 USD
hints: Read two lines: Integer.parseInt for the shillings, Double.parseDouble for the rate.
System.out.printf("%d KSh = %.2f USD%n", ksh, ksh / rate);

exercises.title: The average trap
exercises.prompt: Write average(int a, int b, int c) returning the average as a double. average(1, 2, 2) must be 1.6666666666666667, not 1.0.

tests.hint_if_fail: int / int is whole division. Make it a double first: (a + b + c) / 3.0

hints: The starter divides an int by an int.

exercises.title: Bags needed
exercises.prompt: Write bagsNeeded(int kg) for 90 kg bags: a part-full bag still needs a bag. bagsNeeded(250) is 3, bagsNeeded(180) is 2, bagsNeeded(0) is 0.
hints: Math.ceil rounds up, but it needs a double and returns a double.

quiz.q: What is 9 / 2 in Java when both are ints?

quiz.why: One double operand makes the division a double division. (double)(9/2) divides first and gives 4.0.

quiz.q: Why read lines and convert instead of nextInt()?
choices: Mixing nextInt and nextLine leaves a stray newline that causes skipped input
quiz.why: nextInt leaves the Enter behind; the next nextLine reads an empty line.

cards.q: Read a line of input in Java?
